# Benchmarks

MLX-graphs is compared with [PyTorch Geometric](https://pyg.org) (PyG) on the same Mac, on both PyTorch backends: MPS (the Apple GPU) and CPU. Every framework trains the same models, with the same hyperparameters, on the same data, and the training loss and test accuracy are recorded alongside the times: being faster only counts at the same results.

Each section below is one machine. Click a figure to see it at full size.

## What is measured

- **One layer**: one forward + backward pass of GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, GAT and GATv2 on random graphs of 100k, 500k and 2M edges.
- **Node classification**: full-batch training of GCN, GraphSAGE and GAT on Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, Amazon Photo / Computers, Coauthor CS / Physics and ogbn-arxiv, 3 seeds.
- **Graph classification**: mini-batch training of GCN, GraphSAGE and GIN on the TU datasets MUTAG, PROTEINS, NCI1 and DD, 3 seeds.

The scripts are in [benchmarks/pyg_comparison](https://github.com/mlx-graphs/mlx-graphs/tree/main/benchmarks/pyg_comparison). Its README describes how the comparison is kept fair, and every number of the figures is in a table in the `results.md` file next to them.

## Reproducing

```bash
pip install -e '.[benchmarks]'
python benchmarks/pyg_comparison/run.py    # ~1.5 hours, results/<chip>/<version>/
python benchmarks/pyg_comparison/plot.py   # figures, results.md and this page's section
```

Every configuration runs in its own process under a 16 GB memory cap; a run over the cap is reported as out of memory.
